extraction.name: Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval)
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models using prompts containing verifiable instructions that can be automatically and objectively checked.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by creating prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions, filtering illogical prompts with few-shot prompting, rephrasing prompts for diversity with another few-shot prompting approach, and then manually checking and editing each prompt.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts combined with verifiable instructions; generated prompts are listed in Appendix 6.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Illogical prompts were removed, prompts were rephrased to increase diversity, and responses were transformed during loose evaluation by removing markdown font modifiers, the first line, the last line, and combinations of these transformations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were filtered for illogical cases, rephrased for diversity, and manually checked and edited before use.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are produced automatically by deterministic verification programs that check whether each response follows each verifiable instruction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper discusses false negatives in strict verification and introduces a complementary loose criterion using eight response transformations to reduce false negatives, while noting this may introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Simple heuristics, programming-based deterministic verification, and few-shot prompting
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to improve prompts and verifiable instructions, expand the set of instructions, and support multimodal use cases in future work.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by the importance of reliable instruction following for safety and reliability, especially in high-stakes domains such as healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper argues that human evaluation can introduce biases and inconsistencies, and that model-based evaluation can be biased by evaluator model limitations; IFEval is presented as a more unbiased alternative.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are fully objectively and automatically verifiable; edge cases remain. The current implementation can be improved by increasing the diversity and quantity of instructions and extending to multimodal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for measuring instruction-following ability of large language models and comparing models across instruction types; used to report baseline results for GPT-4 and PaLM 2.

name.evidence: To overcome these issues, we introduce Instruction-Following Eval ( IFEval ) for large language models.

description.evidence: In summary, we propose IFEval: Instruction-Following Eval, a benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions.

url.evidence: Our code and data can be found at https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/instruction_following_eval

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We alleviate these problems by creating our prompts through four steps. First, we generate a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt. Then, we use few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them. As the third step, we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt, to increase the diversity of phrasing. Finally, we manually check and edit the rephrased prompts one by one.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial, not only for the precision of tasks but also for the safety and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: It is important to note that while we focus on verifiable instructions, very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically – there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed... rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In this paper, we introduce IFEval, a new approach for evaluating the proficiency of language models in instruction following... Furthermore, by analyzing the evaluation results, researchers are able to draw insights on what types of instructions are not usually followed, and compare different large language models on various instruction types... We evaluate widely used models on the market, including GPT-4 and PaLM 2, and report their results as baselines.
